messages:
maria: Quick sync — want to vet the streaming handoff microflow before we lock the UI. Noticed a couple of readability and timing issues when the stop button appears mid-stream.

sam: Saw the mock, looks tight. My main worry is visual noise when tokens are dropping in and the stop/regenerate controls slide in. Users might miss the stop affordance. :eyes:

kevin: Agreed. Right now the stop button animates from the right and the token counter jitter makes it feel like things are moving too much. I can reduce the counter reflow, or pin the counter to the left of the toolbar.

maria: Pinning could help. Also thinking about reducing the counter font weight during stream so the message text reads higher priority. We have data that users glance at tokens only after generation completes.

nora: Accessibility note — ensure the stop button has a persistent accessible name. If the label changes to "Stop" then to "Regenerate" visually, screen reader users can get confused. Use aria-live for state changes but stable aria-labels. Example: `button aria-label=\"stream-control-stop\"` and update `aria-pressed`/`data-state`.

kevin: Good call. Proposed snippet for clearer SR state:```html
<button aria-label=\"stream-control-stop\" data-action=\"stop\">Stop</button>
<button aria-label=\"stream-control-regenerate\" data-action=\"regen\">Regenerate</button>
```

sam: Do we want both buttons visible at once? Feels busy. Maybe show Stop during streaming, then reveal Regenerate and a subtle token-summary after completion. Trigger a focus hint for keyboard users when regen appears.

maria: Prefer single primary action during stream (Stop), secondary actions after. But product question — should the token counter remain visible during streaming for users doing cost-awareness? Or hide until completion?

kevin: Technically we can show a collapsed token pill with total so far (e.g., "78 tok") that expands on hover/focus. That keeps layout stable. I'll prototype a low-contrast pill with reduced font-weight during streaming.

nora: Make sure the collapsed pill has at least 3:1 contrast vs background in both collapsed and expanded states. Also tab-order: Stop must be reachable first for keyboard. If the pill opens on focus, don't trap keyboard users.

maria: Copy tweak: instead of "Stop" maybe use "Stop generation" for clarity in small screens where icon-only buttons exist. For icon-only, always include visible tooltip and aria-label.

sam: UX nit — animation timing for the handoff feels too fast. Users don't notice the transition when stream finishes and regen appears. Slow the opacity transition to 160ms and add a 40ms delay for the token pill to avoid competing motion.

kevin: I'll implement 160ms ease-out for the toolbar and a separate 40ms stagger for the pill. Also will add `prefers-reduced-motion` checks.

maria: Prompt library placement: current mock has shelf on the right. Some PMs prefer left rail for easier reach on large monitors. Thoughts?

sam: Right shelf is okay but when the playground is narrow the shelf overlays the token/controls. Could we float the shelf as a drawer that pushes content and collapses on smaller widths?

kevin: Drawer approach works. On mobile collapse to bottom sheet. Also remove pointer events from underlying stream area while prompt picker animates in.

nora: Ensure focus management: when the prompt drawer opens, move focus to first interactive element inside, and return focus to the invoking control on close. Announce via polite aria-live region: "Prompt drawer opened".

maria: Great checklist. Can you action, @kevin — small prototype + small screen screenshots? Sam, can you update mocks with reduced weight counter and the 160ms timing? Nora, can you add the a11y checklist bullets in the ticket?

designbot: Created ticket #PL-4921: "Streaming handoff: stop/regenerate timing, token pill, prompt drawer a11y" and added checklist items.

kevin: On it. Will post prototype link and screenshots by EOD.

sam: Thanks — will update before Figma handoff. :thumbsup:
